title: Lesson 1: All From 9, Last From 10 — Fast Addition Trick
learningGoals: Understand that every digit has a complement that makes a round number.
Apply the sutra 'All From 9, Last From 10' to find complements instantly.
coreIdeas: All digits from 9 except the last digit which comes from 10.
This sutra removes borrowing entirely from round-number subtraction.
Speed comes from recognising the pattern, not from carrying.

workedExamples.method: Last digit from 10: 10−7=3. Other digit from 9: 9−3=6. Answer: 63.
Last digit from 10: 10−6=4. Others from 9: 9−2=7, 9−4=5. Answer: 754.
Last digit from 10: 10−1=9. Others from 9: 9−3=6, 9−5=4, 9−2=7. Answer: 6479.

starterPractice: Warm-up: What is the complement of 7 to make 10?
Guided: Use All From 9, Last From 10 to find 100 − 43.

onboarding.coachIntro: Hi! I am Raj, your Vedic Maths coach. Today you will learn a super trick that lets you subtract from 100 or 1000 in just two seconds — no borrowing ever!
onboarding.placementRule: Start at beginner level. If the learner gets complement pairs instantly, skip the warm-up and go straight to 2-digit complements.

mission.missionPromise: Master the complement sutra and subtract from round numbers at lightning speed.
mission.successCelebration: Amazing! You have cracked the complement code. No more borrowing for you!

microLessonPattern: Coach names the sutra and gives one punchy example.
Board shows the rule visually with colour highlights.
Student reads the rule aloud before trying.
Student attempts the question before the answer appears.
Instant feedback celebrates or pinpoints the exact wrong digit.
Review prompt checks if the student can state the rule from memory.

rewardLoop.xpUnit: Award 10 to 18 XP per exercise group based on difficulty.
rewardLoop.streakRule: Keep the streak counter visible; a correct answer on retry still counts as streak-save.
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Each group earns a themed badge tied to the complement skill being practiced.
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Short coach cheer, XP pulse animation, and progress bar moves forward.

reviewLoop.trigger: Two wrong answers in one group triggers a mini re-teach with a smaller number.
reviewLoop.practiceStyle: Re-show the worked board step, then give a simpler number to try.
reviewLoop.masteryRule: Advance only after the student answers the checkpoint correctly.
reviewLoop.revisitRule: Missed groups reappear at the start of the next session as warm-up cards.

uiDirectives.noScrollGoal: Student sees mission progress, question card, and action buttons without scrolling.
